description: We’re a team exploring how NASA’s Mars data can be transformed into practical, science-driven tools for human exploration. Our goal is to make complex scientific information more accessible and useful to astronauts, supporting informed decisions, mission adaptability, and safer exploration of the Martian surface.
summary:
HADID (Mission Intelligence) is an interactive, layered decision-support tool designed to support future human exploration of Jezero Crater on Mars. Inspired by Perseverance's discovery of potential biosignatures, HADID aims to help identify scientifically promising locations for future sample collection.

The tool brings together geological, mineralogical, and environmental information into one interactive interface. Users can explore different data layers, examine scientific points of interest, and compare proposed exploration routes and sample-collection strategies.

HADID addresses the challenge of making complex and scattered Martian datasets easier to access, visualize, and interpret. By combining different types of scientific information in one place, it provides a clearer understanding of the exploration area and helps users evaluate locations of scientific interest.

Its goal is to support more informed exploration decisions and contribute to the planning of future human missions to Mars.
details:
HADID is an interactive, layered decision-support tool designed to support future human exploration of Jezero Crater on Mars. It brings together geological, mineralogical, and environmental information in one interface, allowing users to explore data layers, examine scientific points of interest, and compare proposed exploration routes and sample-collection strategies.

Inspired by Perseverance’s discovery of potential biosignatures, HADID aims to help astronauts identify scientifically promising locations for future sample collection. Making complex and scattered Martian datasets easier to access and interpret.

We developed the prototype using Figma Make, combining interface design, interactive mapping, and data visualization. The project draws on NASA’s Mars exploration datasets and resources.

Key factors considered included scientific relevance, data availability, environmental conditions, usability, and the limitations of existing mission data. HADID is currently a prototype, and its proposed routes and strategies are conceptual rather than validated navigation plans.
